To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GAP-43 and/or SCG10 mRNAS were expressed in the excitatoy relay neurons of the LGN in an actiity dependent manner.

both GAP- 43 and SCG 10 mRNAs (1) are expressed in most neurons in the LGNs of normal macaque monkeys, (2) are not expressed in inhibitory GABA-ergic interneurons in LGN, (3) are downregulated in the deprived LGNs of macaque monkeys deprived of monovular visual input, and (4) are expressed in inhibitory perigeniculate neurons that project to relay neurons of LGN.
the expression of GAP43 and SCG 10 mRNAs was regulated in an activity-dependent fashion in relay neurons in the lateral geneculate nucleus of monkeys.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of GAP43 and SCG 10 mRNAs.
the development and maintenance of the visual system in the macaque monkey, using nonradioactive in situ hybridization histochemistry.
the expression of mRNAs of growth-associated proteins (GAP-43 and SC-10) in the lateral genieulate nucleus (LNG) of normal and monocularly deprived macaque monkeys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the two growth-associated proteins GAP-43 and SGC10 are expressed in the relay neurons in the monkey LGN and that the expression of both mRNAs is downregulated after monocular deprivation, indicating that both GAP- and SCG10-encoding genes are regulated by activity in the monkey LGNs.
GAP-43 and/or SCG10 are expressed in all types of neurons in the LGNs of both normal and monocularly deprived macaques.
GAP-43 and/or SCG10 mRNA expression is regulated in the LGN by visual activity, and that this regulation occurs in the excitatory neurons of the LGN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GAP-43 and/or SCG10 mRNAS are expressed in the relay neurons in the thalamus, which receive visual input from the retina.
the activity-dependent expression of GAP-143 and SCG10 mRNA in the LGN is a mechanism that regulates the synaptic plasticity of relay neurons in the monkey LGN.
both GAP- 43 and SCG 10 mRNAs can be used as markers to identify relay neurons in the monkey LGN.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of GAP43 and SCG-10 mRNAs can be used to label the excitatory relay cells in the monkey LGN, and that these mRNAs are regulated by visual input in an activity-dependent fashion.
GAP-43 and/or SCG10 mNAs are expressed in all three classes of relay neurons of the LGN.
GAP-43 and/or SCG10 are expressed in relay cells, but not interneurons, of the LGN.
